log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 51% BRING: dragapult, 17% BRING: metagross, 13% BRING: rotomwash
Pick 2: 34% BRING: garchomp, 30% BRING: metagross, 20% BRING: rotomwash
Pick 3: 52% BRING: metagross, 22% BRING: rotomwash, 17% BRING: scizor

Incineroar is mandatory for Intimidate and Fake Out pressure into Scizor and Metagross, the likely physical Steel leads. Dragonite gives priority ExtremeSpeed and Ice Punch to revenge the faster Dragapult and Garchomp. Gholdengo blocks Toxapex status and hits Dragapult and Metagross super-effectively with Shadow Ball.

decisions.thought: 95% MOVE: dracometeor, 2% SWITCH: garchomp, 2% SWITCH: metagross

Fake Out is immune into Dragapult and Flare Blitz is resisted, so Incineroar is in a bad matchup to stay in. Intimidate dropped its Attack, proving it isn't Clear Body, so Parting Shot will weaken it further and pivot safely.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating type matchups and move effectiveness to choose the optimal first turn against Dragapult.Assessing Parting Shot interaction with Clear Body and evaluating Gholdengo as a defensive pivot.Evaluating Parting Shot versus direct switch while confirming ability and type matchups.

decisions.thought: Parting Shot forces us out into a debuffed Dragapult. Gholdengo is the bad matchup to avoid losing, since Good as Gold blocks Will-O-Wisp/Thunder Wave and it resists Dragon to preserve Dragonite's Multiscale.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing Pokémon battle rules to select the single best turn action within format and output constraints.Evaluating opponent team composition and move legality to pick the optimal action under format constraints.Comparing dragonite and gholdengo switch options against a debuffed dragapult and likely opponent pivots.Evaluating Gholdengo's status immunity versus Dragonite's Multiscale preservation for the next pivot.

decisions.thought: 72% MOVE: phantomforce, 14% MOVE: shadowball, 10% SWITCH: garchomp
Dragapult moves first but is at -3 SpA after Draco Meteor into Parting Shot, so it cannot threaten Gholdengo. It will likely switch out, giving a free setup turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing turn constraints and selecting the single best legal action based on speed, knockout potential, or matchup.Evaluating legal actions against a weakened dragapult and selecting shadowball for super effective damage.

decisions.thought: 100% MOVE: phantomforce
Dragapult vanished with Phantom Force last turn and is faster, so it will strike first this turn. Protect blocks that hit and preserves our +2 boost.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing Pokemon turn mechanics to determine that Protect blocks the incoming Phantom Force hit.

decisions.thought: 87% MOVE: phantomforce, 6% SWITCH: garchomp, 3% SWITCH: metagross
Dragapult is faster but at -2 Attack and -3 Sp. Atk, so Gholdengo should survive a hit. A +2 super-effective Shadow Ball is a likely knockout on 80% Dragapult.

decisions.thought: 100% MOVE: phantomforce

Dragapult vanished last turn so Shadow Ball missed, but it must strike now and is hittable. It moves first, yet at -2 Attack Gholdengo should survive the Phantom Force and KO back with +2 STAB super effective Shadow Ball.

decisions.thought: 73% SWITCH: garchomp, 27% SWITCH: metagross
70% MOVE: earthquake, 29% MOVE: earthquake [MEGA], 0% SWITCH: metagross
Gholdengo is slower than Garchomp and will likely be knocked out by Earthquake before it can attack. This is a bad matchup to stay in, so switch to Dragonite which is immune to Ground.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating type matchups and damage to decide whether Gholdengo can survive and KO Garchomp.Assessing Dragonite's Multiscale and speed advantage versus Garchomp as a safer switch than Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: 71% MOVE: stoneedge [MEGA], 16% MOVE: stoneedge, 7% MOVE: dragonclaw [MEGA]
Ice Punch is 4x super effective and should knockout Garchomp. Multiscale at full HP guarantees survival even if Garchomp is faster with Rock coverage. Don't Mega yet to keep Multiscale for this hit.

decisions.thought: 77% SWITCH: metagross, 17% MOVE: stoneedge, 6% MOVE: dragonclaw
Garchomp at 8% will KO low Dragonite with Stone Edge if it moves first. Extreme Speed has +2 priority and guarantees the knockout regardless of speed. Mega Evolve to boost its power.

decisions.thought: 90% MOVE: meteormash, 4% MOVE: bulletpunch, 4% MOVE: zenheadbutt

Dragonite cannot KO 87% Metagross with Earthquake and dies to any hit, so this is a bad matchup to stay in. Preserving ExtremeSpeed to pick off 8% Garchomp is key. Incineroar pivots with Intimidate and threatens Flare Blitz.

decisions.thought: 42% MOVE: meteormash, 37% MOVE: stealthrock, 17% MOVE: zenheadbutt
Metagross moves first but is at -1 from Intimidate and Meteor Mash is not very effective, so Incineroar survives easily. Flare Blitz is super effective and should knock out the 87% Metagross.

decisions.thought: 100% SWITCH: garchompmega
100% MOVE: earthquake, 0% MOVE: stoneedge, 0% MOVE: swordsdance

Incineroar is slower than Mega Garchomp and at 15 HP will be knocked out before moving. Staying in to attack sacrifices Incineroar for a free revenge kill rather than risking Gholdengo or Dragonite on a switch.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is immune to Earthquake and has Extreme Speed priority to finish the 8% Garchomp. Gholdengo is weak to Earthquake and may be outsped and knocked out. Priority knockout is the deciding factor.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating the optimal switch between two bench Pokémon against a low-HP opponent with known moves.Assessing damage ranges and type matchups to rule out a safe switch.

decisions.thought: 78% MOVE: dragonclaw, 20% MOVE: stoneedge, 2% MOVE: earthquake
Opponent Garchomp is at 8% HP, so any hit knocks it out and wins the game. Extremespeed has priority to guarantee we move first.
